cells.tense: Right now you can stand in front of something you don't understand yet and let it stay that way for a while.
cells.act: keep the motivation warm with steady care
cells.ask: Give something that already matters to you ten unhurried minutes today — attention all the way in, no conclusion at the end. Nothing else is asked of you.
cells.core:
Something catches you before you can put a name to it, and you're willing to stay near it while it's still unclear. You can hold your attention on a thing without needing to justify why it earned that, and things get to mean something to you before they can be explained.

What feeds this is smaller than it sounds. Choose something that already matters — not a new project, something you can feel is yours — and give it ten minutes of real care today. Unhurried. No conclusion waiting at the end. You're not trying to figure it out. You're keeping warm something already alive in your attention, and a fire tended steadily holds. You'll feel the difference in how you hold it, and that holding is the point.
cells.sheetLine: You know what deserves your attention before you can explain why.
cells.verb: opening to what isn't known yet with fresh eyes
cells.place: where you know what deserves your attention before you can put it into words

cells.tense: You're bracing for a feeling that hasn't arrived, and what's coming next is getting its plan drawn before it lands.
cells.act: care for it with fresh hands and see what it needs
cells.ask: Look after something that already works — a routine, a plant, a corner of your week that runs fine — exactly as it is for a few days. Nothing to fix.
cells.core:
You're running ahead of what's actually here, feeling a thing out before it has happened and drafting your response in advance. Some of that is just sensitivity. Most of it means your hands are full of next month, and it's hard to hold what's actually in reach when they are. The future gets written before it shows up.

There's a way back that's plainer than the feeling. Take something that already works — a routine that's running, a plant that's alive, a corner of your week that doesn't need saving — and look after it exactly at its present size. No upgrades, no repairs it didn't ask for. Do that for a few days and watch how much of your attention is going to rescuing things that aren't in trouble. Fresh hands notice what a thing actually needs, which is usually less than you'd guess from here.
cells.sheetLine: You're fixing things that aren't in trouble yet.
cells.verb: opening to what isn't known yet with fresh eyes
cells.place: where you know what deserves your attention before you can put it into words

cells.tense: The door you're standing in front of was closed some time back, and your hand is still on it.
cells.act: follow a raw curiosity with no use for it
cells.ask: Follow a small curiosity for a few days with nothing it has to feed — read it, look it up, ask the question — and stop there, with no output.
cells.core:
What used to land clean needs a reason bolted on before you'll trust it now. Nothing arrives without one. Whatever you're picking up about a room, a person, a piece of work — it comes through slower, and it asks permission from the part of you that wants evidence first.

Go sideways at it. Find something you're genuinely curious about, with no use for it and nothing it has to feed, and follow that for a few days. No writeup, no reason given to anyone. You're not trying to get back what was lost. You're giving the part of you that receives something to receive without having to justify itself. Attention tends to come back through that side entrance, not the front one.
cells.sheetLine: You trust what you know only once it has a reason.
cells.verb: opening to what isn't known yet with fresh eyes
cells.place: where you know what deserves your attention before you can put it into words

cells.tense: The work is already happening, and when anyone asks how you got there you say you were guessing.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Take one call you made recently that turned out well, and put the sequence of it on paper — the steps in order, no feelings, no explanations. Just what you did.
cells.core:
You can tell which way to move before you can defend the direction, and you move. Then someone asks how you knew and you say you guessed, got lucky, followed a feeling. The calls are yours. The name on them isn't.

Try it this way instead. Choose one decision from the past month that worked out, and set down how you got there. The steps, in order, plain — no explanations, no feelings, nothing about instincts or gut. Just what you did, one line after another, until it's on the page. What you'll find is a method. Not a mood, not a hunch, but a sequence you followed and can follow again. Nothing here needs proving to anyone. You're reading your own handwriting for once.
cells.sheetLine: The calls are yours and you file them under luck.
cells.verb: opening to what isn't known yet with fresh eyes
cells.place: where you know what deserves your attention before you can put it into words
